sources.title: ByteDance backend interview note exact array predicate prompt

claims.text: The source asks for values smaller than all preceding elements and larger than all following elements; endpoint empty-side behavior is not stated.
For an internal position, the predicate is equivalent to value < left prefix minimum and value > right suffix maximum.
The strict implementation excluding endpoints matches an independent quadratic oracle on six fixed and 5000 randomized arrays.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=6 randomized=5000 oracle=quadratic-strict endpoints=excluded duplicates=strict

boundary_tests.expected: no match because equality violates strict comparison
no match under explicit non-empty-left-and-right contract
linear implementation exactly matches independent quadratic oracle

findings: The repository source is a single recoverable Coding prompt requiring values smaller than every preceding element and larger than every following element.
The source does not define endpoint truth semantics, so the candidate explicitly limits the implementation contract to internal positions instead of inventing a hidden rule.
The strict all-left/all-right predicate is correctly reduced to comparison with the left prefix minimum and right suffix maximum.
The Java candidate is complete and runnable, with the prefix minimum updated after each position and suffixMax[i+1] excluding the current value.
Equal values are rejected under strict comparisons.
Six fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized arrays agree with an independent O(n^2) oracle.
No generic placeholder implementation or fabricated project experience remains.
